\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{بقشيش} (baqshīsh)}{بقشيش (baqshīsh)}]{\ar{بقشيش} (baqshīsh) — a tip (for service)}

\label{lesson:AR-C446-baqshish}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to slow down, then the Arabic for to hamper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{بقشيش}}
\textbf{\ar{بقشيش}} — \emph{baqshīsh} — \textquotedblleft{}a tip (for service)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ترك} \ar{أبي} \ar{بقشيشا} \ar{للنادل}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{taraka abī baqshīshan li-n-nādil.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father left a tip for the waiter.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{بقشيش}} (\emph{baqshīsh}) was borrowed from Persian \emph{bakhshish}, \textquotedblleft{}a gift\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baqshīsh}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baqshīsh}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{taraka abī baqshīshan li-n-nādil.} — My father left a tip for the waiter.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to slow down, then the Arabic for to hamper, then say \emph{baqshīsh} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{بقشيش} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A tip (for service)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\label{lesson:AR-C446-khidma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to hamper, then the Arabic for a tip.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خدمة}}
\textbf{\ar{خدمة}} — \emph{khidma} — \textquotedblleft{}a service\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كانت} \ar{الخدمة} \ar{في} \ar{المطعم} \ar{ممتازة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kānat al-khidma fī al-maṭʿam mumtāza.}

\textbf{\ar{خدمة}} (\emph{khidma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-d-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to serve\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{خدم} (khadama)}{خدم (khadama)}]{\ar{خدم} (khadama) — to serve; to wait on}

\label{lesson:AR-C446-khadama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a tip, then the Arabic for a service.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{خدم}}
\textbf{\ar{خدم}} — \emph{khadama} — \textquotedblleft{}to serve; to wait on\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{خدمنا} \ar{نادل} \ar{لطيف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{khadamanā nādil laṭīf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A kind waiter served us.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يخدم}, \emph{yakhdum}.

Lane gives the present both as \emph{yakhdumu} and \emph{yakhdimu}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{خدم}} (\emph{khadama}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{kh-d-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to serve\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is the plain verb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رحب} (raḥḥaba)}{رحب (raḥḥaba)}]{\ar{رحب} (raḥḥaba) — to greet warmly; to welcome}

\label{lesson:AR-C446-rahhaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a service, then the Arabic for to serve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رحب}}
\textbf{\ar{رحب}} — \emph{raḥḥaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to greet warmly; to welcome\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رحب} \ar{بنا} \ar{موظف} \ar{الاستقبال}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raḥḥaba binā muwaẓẓaf al-istiqbāl.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The receptionist greeted us warmly.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يرحب}, \emph{yuraḥḥib}.

It takes \emph{bi-}: \emph{raḥḥaba bi-}, \textquotedblleft{}to welcome someone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رحب}} (\emph{raḥḥaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-ḥ-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to be wide, spacious\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, \textquotedblleft{}to make room for a guest\textquotedblright{}; \emph{marḥaban}, \textquotedblleft{}welcome\textquotedblright{}, shares the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raḥḥaba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raḥḥaba binā muwaẓẓaf al-istiqbāl.} — The receptionist greeted us warmly.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a service, then the Arabic for to serve, then say \emph{raḥḥaba} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أوصى} (awṣā)}{أوصى (awṣā)}]{\ar{أوصى} (awṣā) — to recommend}

\label{lesson:AR-C446-awsa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to serve, then the Arabic for to greet warmly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{أوصى}}
\textbf{\ar{أوصى}} — \emph{awṣā} — \textquotedblleft{}to recommend\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{أوصانا} \ar{المرشد} \ar{بمطعم} \ar{صغير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{awṣānā al-murshid bi-maṭʿam ṣaghīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The guide recommended a small restaurant to us.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يوصي}, \emph{yūṣī}.

It takes \emph{bi-} before the thing recommended.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{أوصى}} (\emph{awṣā}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{w-ṣ-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to join; to enjoin\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form IV.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.

\section[(dialogue)]{Words from chapters 439–446 — a review}

\label{lesson:AR-R446-review-439-446}



\begin{quote}
Say the Arabic for a view and a tower.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a view, a tower, a monument, to explore, to take along
  \item a fountain, a souvenir, a rest stop, to accompany, to give a lift
  \item reception, a hotel guest, a residence, to depart from, to vacate
  \item a campsite, a resort, a chalet, to set alight, pine trees
  \item a doorman, a bed sheet, cleanliness, to overlook, a strongbox
  \item electricity, to heat up, to be cut off, an adapter, to light up
  \item a tram, a lorry, a steering wheel, to slow down, to hamper
  \item a tip, a service, to serve, to greet warmly, to recommend
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A view? (\textbf{\ar{منظر}}, \emph{manẓar}.) A tower? (\textbf{\ar{برج}}, \emph{burj}.) A monument? (\textbf{\ar{نصب}}, \emph{nuṣb}.) To explore? (\textbf{\ar{استكشف}}, \emph{istakshafa}.) To take along? (\textbf{\ar{اصطحب}}, \emph{iṣṭaḥaba}.) A fountain? (\textbf{\ar{نافورة}}, \emph{nāfūra}.) A souvenir? (\textbf{\ar{تذكار}}, \emph{tidhkār}.) A rest stop? (\textbf{\ar{استراحة}}, \emph{istirāḥa}.) To accompany? (\textbf{\ar{رافق}}, \emph{rāfaqa}.) To give a lift? (\textbf{\ar{أوصل}}, \emph{awṣala}.) Reception? (\textbf{\ar{استقبال}}, \emph{istiqbāl}.) A hotel guest? (\textbf{\ar{نزيل}}, \emph{nazīl}.) A residence? (\textbf{\ar{إقامة}}, \emph{iqāma}.) To depart from? (\textbf{\ar{غادر}}, \emph{ghādara}.) To vacate? (\textbf{\ar{أخلى}}, \emph{akhlā}.) A campsite? (\textbf{\ar{مخيم}}, \emph{mukhayyam}.) A resort? (\textbf{\ar{منتجع}}, \emph{muntajaʿ}.) A chalet? (\textbf{\ar{شاليه}}, \emph{shālīh}.) To set alight? (\textbf{\ar{أشعل}}, \emph{ashʿala}.) Pine trees? (\textbf{\ar{صنوبر}}, \emph{ṣanawbar}.) A doorman? (\textbf{\ar{بواب}}, \emph{bawwāb}.) A bed sheet? (\textbf{\ar{ملاءة}}, \emph{mulāʾa}.) Cleanliness? (\textbf{\ar{نظافة}}, \emph{naẓāfa}.) To overlook? (\textbf{\ar{أطل}}, \emph{aṭalla}.) A strongbox? (\textbf{\ar{خزنة}}, \emph{khazna}.) Electricity? (\textbf{\ar{كهرباء}}, \emph{kahrabāʾ}.) To heat up? (\textbf{\ar{سخن}}, \emph{sakhkhana}.) To be cut off? (\textbf{\ar{انقطع}}, \emph{inqaṭaʿa}.) An adapter? (\textbf{\ar{محول}}, \emph{muḥawwil}.) To light up? (\textbf{\ar{أنار}}, \emph{anāra}.) A tram? (\textbf{\ar{ترام}}, \emph{trām}.) A lorry? (\textbf{\ar{شاحنة}}, \emph{shāḥina}.) A steering wheel? (\textbf{\ar{مقود}}, \emph{miqwad}.) To slow down? (\textbf{\ar{تمهل}}, \emph{tamahhala}.) To hamper? (\textbf{\ar{عرقل}}, \emph{ʿarqala}.) A tip? (\textbf{\ar{بقشيش}}, \emph{baqshīsh}.) A service? (\textbf{\ar{خدمة}}, \emph{khidma}.) To serve? (\textbf{\ar{خدم}}, \emph{khadama}.) To greet warmly? (\textbf{\ar{رحب}}, \emph{raḥḥaba}.) To recommend? (\textbf{\ar{أوصى}}, \emph{awṣā}.)
